NDT training across inland Texas: how it works for employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT trains inland Texas technicians and crews to ASNT SNT-TC-1A in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I, II and III. Theory runs live online for individuals anywhere from San Antonio to El Paso; company groups are trained onsite at the employer's facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice. There is no Atlantis training centre in any Texas city: training comes to your site or your screen.

This page is the regional hub for inland Texas. It links to every inland Texas city training page we publish, explains how the main industries away from the coast use NDT, sets out the radiography licensing and certification rules that apply across the state, and answers the questions employers in San Antonio, Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth, the Permian Basin and El Paso ask most often. If you are on the coast, start with the Gulf Coast refining corridor hub instead. For the whole state, see the Texas NDT training hub.

San Antonio has its own NDT training page

If you searched for NDT training in San Antonio, the page you want is NDT training in San Antonio. It covers the courses, certification path, delivery options and FAQs specific to San Antonio employers and technicians. San Antonio's NDT work is driven by aviation maintenance and military aircraft support around Port San Antonio and Joint Base San Antonio, automotive manufacturing at the Toyota truck plant on the South Side, and oil and gas work reaching into the Eagle Ford shale to the south. Aviation employers there should also read aviation NDT training in San Antonio, and trainees can rehearse methods on Practical NDT for San Antonio. Employers who need Level III support rather than training can go to NDT consulting in San Antonio.

The San Antonio page carries the city detail. This hub stays at the regional level, so that each city's searchers land on the page written for their city.

The sub-regions in more detail

San Antonio and south-central Texas

Port San Antonio, on the former Kelly Air Force Base, hosts aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul operations alongside the training and flying missions of Joint Base San Antonio. Aviation NDT here is dominated by eddy current, ultrasonic and penetrant inspection of airframes, engines and components, and employers commonly run personnel programmes to NAS 410 alongside or instead of SNT-TC-1A. Toyota's truck plant and its on-site suppliers bring weld and component inspection, and the Eagle Ford shale to the south brings pipeline and production work. Full detail is on the San Antonio training page.

Austin and central Texas

Central Texas has become one of the largest construction markets in the country for advanced manufacturing. Samsung's semiconductor fab in Taylor, Tesla's gigafactory east of Austin and the supplier plants around them need structural steel welds inspected to AWS D1.1 and process and high-purity piping examined under ASME B31.3. Testing agencies and contractors working these projects need VT, UT, MT, RT and PT technicians certified under a written practice. See the Austin training page.

Dallas-Fort Worth

The Metroplex combines two economies. Fort Worth is home to large military aircraft and rotorcraft manufacturers, including Lockheed Martin's F-35 production and Bell's headquarters, plus aviation MRO at the region's airports, all of which use ET, UT, PAUT and PT at Level II and Level III. Dallas hosts the headquarters of major pipeline and midstream operators and of rail car manufacturer Trinity Industries, along with a deep fabrication base. The Barnett Shale to the west adds gas gathering and compression. See Dallas and Fort Worth.

Midland, Odessa and the Permian Basin

The Permian Basin is the most intensive oilfield NDT market in the country. Operators, midstream companies and service contractors need RT and UT crews for pipeline girth welds under API 1104, PAUT for automated weld inspection, UT thickness surveys on gathering lines and tank batteries, and MT and PT on fabricated equipment. Midland carries more of the operator and engineering offices; Odessa more of the service yards and fabrication shops. The Midland, Odessa and Permian Basin pages cover the detail, and refinery work in the wider region at Big Spring is covered on the refining pages linked above.

El Paso and far west Texas

El Paso combines a refinery, the large Fort Bliss installation, rail yards and a manufacturing economy tied closely to plants across the border in Ciudad Juarez. That mix means UT, RT, MT and PT for refinery turnarounds, VT and MT for fabrication and rail, and ET and PT for aviation and component work. See the El Paso training page.

Radiography licensing and certification in Texas

Texas is an NRC Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, and its industrial radiography rule sets requirements for radiographers and radiographer trainees working under a Texas licence. That applies statewide, from Permian pipeline crews to fabrication shops in the Metroplex. In practice:

  • the employer holds the radioactive-materials licence, or works under a licence that authorises its radiography;
  • radiographers and trainees must meet DSHS training, certification and personnel-monitoring requirements in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification;
  • SNT-TC-1A RT training covers radiation-safety principles, but it does not replace the state's radiographer certification or the employer's licence conditions.

Confirm the current requirements with DSHS before an RT crew mobilises. Atlantis does not claim state approval for any training course. Work at refineries and gas plants also brings site safety orientation and access requirements set by the owner.

SNT-TC-1A certification path for inland Texas technicians

Inland Texas employers almost all certify technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, an employer-based system. The steps are the same in every city on this page:

  1. The employer's written practice sets the training hours, experience, examinations and vision requirements for each method and level. If you don't have one, or it is out of date, see written practice development.
  2. Formal training in the method and level, delivered live online, onsite or blended. The recommended minimums by method and level are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience logged in the method under supervision, documented in a form an auditor can trace.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations administered by a Level III, with the practical on real specimens.
  5. Vision examination, near vision and colour contrast, on the schedule the written practice sets.
  6. Certification by the employer, followed by recertification on the written practice's cycle.

More on the framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification and the SNT-TC-1A certification programme for employers.

Local options compared, honestly

Inland Texas technicians have several routes into NDT, and the right one depends on where you are in your career.

  • Public technical colleges. Texas State Technical College's welding programmes include NDT and quality-control content, which suits people entering the trade through welding. Community colleges across the region run welding and industrial-technology programmes; check each college's current catalogue for NDT content.
  • ASNT local sections. ASNT sections in Texas run technical meetings and networking events, useful for anyone building a career or preparing for Level III.
  • Employer in-house programmes. Larger operators, service companies and manufacturers train and certify under their own written practices, often with an outside Level III.
  • Atlantis NDT. SNT-TC-1A training led by an ASNT Level III, delivered live online for individuals and onsite at your facility for crews, with written-practice and Level III support for the employer. We do not run a walk-in school; we fit training around your work schedule and your site.

Online, onsite and blended delivery for inland Texas crews

Distances in inland Texas make delivery choices matter. A crew in Odessa and a lab in Fort Worth are a long drive apart, and pulling technicians off the job for a week of classroom time is expensive in lost work. Our delivery options:

  • Live online theory, instructor-led, for individuals and small groups anywhere in the region. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility, using your equipment, your procedures and your parts, under ASNT Level III oversight. This suits Permian service yards, Metroplex fabrication shops and aviation hangars alike. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended: online theory first, then a shorter onsite block for hands-on training and practical examinations.

Scheduling works around drilling and completion activity in the Permian, turnaround windows at El Paso and the other inland refineries, and production schedules at manufacturing plants. Ask about onsite training for your inland Texas crew; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Level III services for inland Texas NDT companies

Many inland Texas inspection companies and fabricators are too small to employ a full-time Level III but still need one to sign the written practice, approve procedures and administer examinations. Atlantis provides ASNT Level III services for that situation, including Level III of record arrangements; see ASNT Level III consulting services and NDT consulting in Texas. Technicians aiming for Level III themselves can start at ASNT Level III training.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The last three map directly to inland Texas work. It is a practice tool only and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in inland Texas

Where can I get NDT training in San Antonio?

Atlantis delivers NDT training for San Antonio technicians live online and for employers onsite at their facility. Full detail is on the San Antonio NDT training page.

Do you have a training centre in Dallas, Austin, Midland or El Paso?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in any Texas city. Individuals train live online; company groups are trained onsite at their own facility.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, for theory. Certification under SNT-TC-1A also needs on-the-job experience and practical examinations on real specimens, administered under your employer's written practice.

How do I get NDT certified in inland Texas?

Complete the training, experience, examinations and vision test your employer's written practice requires; your employer then certifies you. The training requirements matrix lists recommended training and experience by method and level.

Do I need a Texas licence to do radiography?

Radiography in Texas is done under a licence issued by the DSHS Radiation Control Program, and radiographers and trainees must meet its certification and training requirements. Confirm current rules with DSHS.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in the Permian Basin?

RT and UT for pipeline welds, PAUT for automated weld inspection, UT thickness surveys, and MT and PT on fabricated equipment. See the Permian Basin training page.

What NDT do aviation employers in San Antonio and Fort Worth need?

Mostly ET, UT, PT, MT and VT at Level II for airframes, engines and components. Many aviation employers run NAS 410 programmes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Can you train our crew at our facility in west Texas?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight is our standard model for crews, including remote Permian locations.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and whether you already hold Level I. Recommended minimum training and experience are listed in the training requirements matrix.

What does NDT training cost in inland Texas?

Quoted on request. The quote depends on the method, level, group size and whether delivery is online or onsite. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or training provider, and Atlantis does not claim that approval. Employer-paid training is the usual route for our courses.

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification accepted by inland Texas employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used personnel-certification framework among US NDT employers. Specific customers may also ask for API, NAS 410 or other schemes, which are outside Atlantis training.
